clue.text: Vehicle loaded with a weight of stones

indicators.note: a cart loaded with something carries it inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle

explanation.surface: A truck carrying a heavy load of rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is not the article of 'a weight': it is the letter put into CART. 'Stones' means gems, not rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A carat is the unit used to weigh gemstones, which jewellers call stones.

clue.text: Bet rail company will change this old carriage

indicators.note: letters that change take a different order, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A railway firm wagers that a vintage carriage will be replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will change' rearranges BET, RAIL and CO into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet was a light two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle with a folding hood.

clue.text: Only half of cast in theatre for rehearsal

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: Only some of the actors are at the theatre for practice.
explanation.walkthrough: Repertory theatre, a company staging a changing programme of plays, is shortened to rep in Britain; 'Only half of' takes the first two letters of 'cast'.
explanation.definitionFit: A recap is a summary that goes over things again, a rehearsal in the sense of a retelling.

clue.text: Quiet performance including revised version of Act I

indicators.note: including means holding within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act on stage

indicators.note: a revised version has its letters reworked, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A subdued show featuring a rewritten first act of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR read 'Act I' as 'Act!'; the page prints Act I, the first act of a play. 'revised version of' rearranges those four letters, and 'including' puts them into the performance word.
explanation.definitionFit: Taciturn means reserved and saying little, a synonym of quiet.

clue.text: With expedition, insured by first-class mail?

definitions.meaning: with speed, as fast as possible
whimsically, haste guaranteed by sending something by fast letter delivery

explanation.surface: Something sent quickly and safely by the best postal service.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means with all speed, originally from letters marked to be carried quickly by couriers.

clue.text: Power given to old-fashioned policeman

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape it anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traditional bobby is given authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' reads as one adjective, but 'fashioned' rearranges OLD into LOD. PLOD is British slang for the police, from Mr Plod in the Noddy books.
explanation.definitionFit: Plod is British slang for a police officer, after the Noddy character Mr Plod.

clue.text: Fish needing space — some stream in here

parts.note: a school is a group of fish
room means space

explanation.surface: Fish need space, and some swim up a stream into this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stream' is not a river: British schools stream pupils into ability groups, taught in a classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils sorted into an ability stream are taught in a classroom.

clue.text: Hesitates, as husband, to maintain son

parts.note: to aver is to maintain or assert

explanation.surface: A man dithers, choosing to stand up for his boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To haver is to dither or vacillate, mainly a British and Scots usage.

clue.text: Period for disposing of creatures on sea-bed?

definitions.meaning: the time a product can be kept for sale before it must be sold or thrown out
animals living on the continental shelf, the shallow sea floor off a coast

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means how long goods stay saleable; literally it can mean animals of the continental shelf.

clue.text: Moderate money for support of artistic efforts

parts.note: to ease something is to moderate or lessen it
L stands for pound sterling, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Restrained funding to back the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support of artistic efforts' sounds like arts funding, but it is the stand a painter's canvas rests on.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's frame holds a canvas upright while the artist works.

clue.text: Sponsor material for set piece on stage

parts.note: to back a venture is to sponsor it
cloth is fabric or material

explanation.surface: A patron pays for the fabric used in the theatre's scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted cloth hung at the rear of a stage is part of the scenery, a set piece.

clue.text: Free verse goes in a new direction

indicators.note: free here means released from its order, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Poetry without rhyme or metre takes an experimental turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free verse' reads as one poetic term, but 'Free' is the anagram signal for VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To change course or swing off in another direction is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Attribute that is required to secure male position

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast within, so the outer piece wraps round the others

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
to put something is to position it

explanation.surface: A trait that a man needs to keep his post.
explanation.definitionFit: To impute a quality or fault is to ascribe it to someone, the verb sense of attribute.

clue.text: Sad start to motoring — our fun ruined by new driver

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter
ruined letters are knocked out of shape, so they are rearranged

parts.note: L is for learner, the plate a new driver in Britain displays

explanation.surface: A gloomy day out in the car, spoilt by a novice behind the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges FUN; OUR happens to stay in place. British learner drivers show an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Mournful means full of grief, a synonym of sorrowful.

clue.text: Took advantage of openings for design work

definitions.text: Took advantage of openings for design work

parts.words: Took advantage of openings for design work
parts.note: sounds like seizing opportunities in design, but describes painting a pattern through cut-out holes in a sheet

explanation.surface: A designer seized career opportunities.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorating by applying paint through holes cut in a template makes the pattern.

clue.text: Party speeches in research centre

parts.note: Lab is short for Labour, the British political party
oratory is the art of making speeches, or speeches collectively

explanation.surface: Politicians deliver addresses at a think tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory is a place where scientific research and experiments are carried out.

clue.text: Outstanding account affected by inflation

parts.note: a bill is an account of money due
owing means outstanding, still unpaid

explanation.surface: An unpaid bill grows as prices rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inflation' suggests rising prices, but it means swelling with air, as a sail does.
explanation.definitionFit: Billowing describes a sail or cloud swelling out as it fills with air.

clue.text: Reason to object

definitions.meaning: the faculty of thought, as in losing one's senses
to dislike or take exception, as in 'do you object?'

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the intellect or reason; the verb means to take exception, as in 'I don't care'.

clue.text: Discouraging blunder interrupts incomplete reconciliation

indicators.note: a piece that interrupts another breaks into the middle of it
incomplete means the last letter is missing

parts.note: detente is an easing of tension between nations, a reconciliation
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A dispiriting mistake halts a peace process before it is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' drops the final E of the diplomatic word for an easing of tension; 'interrupts' then breaks the blunder into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deterrent measure is meant to put people off acting, so it is discouraging.

clue.text: Ponder, as referee, about extra time

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outer piece goes round the other

parts.note: to mediate is to act as a referee between parties
T is the abbreviation for time, here an extra letter

explanation.surface: A match official thinks things over before adding stoppage time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts MEDIATE round the extra T. Football fans will read 'extra time' as added minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to think deeply, a synonym of ponder.

clue.text: Inclination to attack

definitions.meaning: to charge with a lance, as a jousting knight does

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a lean or slope; the verb is to charge at an opponent, as in a joust.

clue.text: Home business he split is not well co-ordinated

parts.note: in means at home
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
rent means torn apart, split

explanation.surface: A family firm breaks up because the man at its head lets it fall into disarray.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech or thought that is disjointed and muddled lacks logical connection or organisation.

clue.text: Run across City swindle

indicators.note: one piece lies across the other, spanning it, so it goes round it

parts.note: to flee is to run away
EC is the postcode for the City of London, its financial district

explanation.surface: A con artist escapes through the financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to cheat them out of money, a synonym of swindle.

clue.text: Announce goal set by professional class

parts.note: a pro is a professional
cl is the abbreviation for class
an aim is a goal

explanation.surface: A coach reveals the target for the experts' group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set by' places the goal after the professional class in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim is to declare publicly, a synonym of announce.

clue.text: Corpulent porker's first prize held up

parts.note: a plum is a prize, as in a plum job

indicators.note: first selects the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A fat pig's winning rosette is on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' means placed on top in this down clue: the prize sits above the porker's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump means rounded and fat, a gentler synonym of corpulent.

clue.text: Bearer to provide monarch with sword on belt

parts.note: to gird is to fasten a sword on with a belt
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A sword-bearer arms the king with a blade at his waist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to provide' merely links: provide the monarch with a girded sword gives GIRD then ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A girder is a beam that bears a load in a building, so a bearer in engineering terms.

clue.text: Urge to plunge into river? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside another, here the reverse of what is written

parts.note: a dive is a plunge

explanation.surface: An impulse to leap into the water, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the reverse' swaps the roles 'into' gives: the river goes into the plunge, not the plunge into the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive is an inner urge or motivation, as in a sex drive.

clue.text: Prompt to leave, given notice

parts.note: to go is to leave
an ad is an advertisement or notice

explanation.surface: Being handed one's notice spurs one to quit.
explanation.definitionFit: To goad someone is to urge or spur them into action, a synonym of prompt.

clue.text: Join in fun — it exhilarates

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the following words, spanning their boundaries

explanation.surface: Come and take part in the fun; it is thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to bring or come together, a synonym of join.

clue.text: Possums may not be so alert

definitions.text: Possums may not be so alert

parts.words: Possums may not be so alert
parts.note: a possum famously plays dead, so it does not appear living; the command to be alert says the opposite

explanation.surface: Marsupials are perhaps less watchful than they seem.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'play possum' is to feign death; the answer is an instruction to be alert, which also describes appearing alive.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an order to be quick and alert, while literally appearing living, which a possum faking death avoids.

clue.text: Obstinate, like Napoleon on top

definitions.meaning: stubborn, unwilling to change one's mind
Napoleon is the boar who leads the farm in Orwell's Animal Farm, so a swine is in charge

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means stubborn; read literally it describes a farm with a swine at its head, as in Orwell's novel.

clue.text: Secure a seat for somebody standing

definitions.text: Secure a seat for somebody standing

parts.words: Secure a seat for somebody standing
parts.note: reads like giving up a chair to someone on their feet, but means voting a candidate who stands into parliament

explanation.surface: Finding a chair for someone left on their feet on a train.
explanation.walkthrough: In British elections a candidate 'stands' for a seat in parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To vote a candidate into office, such as a parliamentary seat, is the verb's sense.
